tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: For precise panel line scribing, use RB Productions tools. Hold the scriber at a 45° angle, applying gentle pressure. Start at one end of the panel line, moving the tool along the line in one smooth motion. For deep lines, use the wider RB002 scriber. Always scribe away from delicate parts to avoid damage.

tips.title: Photo-Etch Bending with Eduard Jigs
tips.text: Eduard photo-etch frets come with bending jigs for precise results. Place the fret part in the jig, using tweezers to hold it in place. Gently bend the part over the jig edge using round pliers. Check the angle periodically; if it's 90°, adjust the bending pressure or use a different jig edge.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Brush Cleaner
tips.text: Keep your Iwata airbrush performing smoothly with regular needle cleaning. After each session, use Iwata Airbrush Cleaner to dissolve paint residue. Soak the needle in the cleaner for 15 minutes, then scrub gently with a soft brush. Rinse thoroughly with water and dry before reassembling the airbrush.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya and Kabuki Tapes
tips.text: For accurate masking, use Tamiya Tape for straight edges and Kabuki Tape for curves. Apply Tamiya Tape in long strips, pressing down firmly to prevent paint leaks. For curves, use Kabuki Tape, which stretches to conform to the surface. Overlap tape strips for multiple colors to avoid paint bleeding.

tips.title: Sanding Stick Progression with Arma Hobby
tips.text: Start with Arma Hobby's coarse sanding stick for removing mold seams, then progress to medium and fine for smoothing. Wet-sand with water, applying light pressure in circular motions. Check progress frequently; sanding too much can remove details. Wipe off residue with a damp cloth between grits.
